definitions.text: For the reasons mentioned above scientists have agreed to adopt standard and user-friendly units called SI or System International Units.
It is the standard unit of length. Symbol m is used for metre. Metre is the distance travelled by light in vacuum in about 300 millionth of a second.
Its symbol is kg and it is the standard unit of mass. A block is kept in France which is taken as a standard unit of mass. It is also defined as the mass of 1000 cm³ of water.
It is the standard unit of time with a symbol s. It is the time that elapses during 9,192,631,770 cycles of the radiation produced by the transition between two levels of the cesium-133 atom.

It is represented by K and it is the standard unit of temperature. It is 1/273rd of the thermodynamic temperature of the triple point of water. It is a point at which all the states of water exist at the same time.
It is the base unit of the amount of pure substance and it is denoted by mol. It is defined as having exactly 6.022 × 10²³ particles of a substance.
An error may be defined as the difference between the measured value and the actual value.

In fact, they have errors that naturally occur and these errors are called systematic errors. Systematic errors may be removed by adding or subtracting a constant adjustment given to each measurement. Systematic error affect the accuracy of the measurement.

Another type of error which a student commits during measurement is called a random error. Random error causes one measurement to differ slightly from the next measurement. It comes from unpredictable changes during an experiment.
Accuracy measures how close results are to the true or known value.
The closeness of two or more measurements to each other is called precision.
Apart from these base units, there are other quantities that are mathematically derived from these base units.

formulas.use: Convert temperature from Celsius to kelvin (K in K; °C in °C; 273 is the conversion constant).

formulas.formula: Volume: m³; area: m²; density: kg m⁻³
formulas.use: Recall the SI derived units listed for volume, area and density (volume in m³; area in m²; density in kg m⁻³).
Use the kilo, deci, centi and milli prefixes to express multiples or fractions of a unit; the powers of ten are dimensionless.

fullMarks: For a question about SI, state the relevant benefit clearly: standard units make communication and data sharing easier and reduce conversions.

When listing the five chemistry base units, give each quantity with its correct unit and symbol: length—metre (m), time—second (s), amount of substance—mole (mol), mass—kilogram (kg), temperature—kelvin (K).
For a derived-unit question, show the quantity and its unit together: volume—m³, density—kg m⁻³, area—m².
For temperature conversion, write the formula first, substitute the Celsius value, and give the final answer in K. Use the textbook conversion K = °C + 273.

For an error question, distinguish the types: systematic error affects accuracy and can be adjusted by adding or subtracting a constant; random error varies between measurements and can come from unpredictable changes.

For accuracy and precision, define each separately. Accuracy is closeness to the true or known value; precision is closeness of measurements to one another. State that one does not guarantee the other.
Write unit symbols correctly and do not pluralize them: use kg, m, s and cm³, not kgs, ms or cm³s.
mistakes: Mixing up accuracy and precision. Fix: accuracy means closeness to the true value; precision means closeness of repeated measurements to one another.
Saying random errors are constant or affect every reading in the same way. Fix: random errors make readings differ unpredictably.
Saying systematic error affects precision only. Fix: systematic error affects accuracy and may be corrected by a constant adjustment.
Writing the Celsius-to-kelvin conversion backwards or giving the answer in °C. Fix: use K = °C + 273 and label the answer K.
Using the wrong base-unit symbol, such as K for kilogram or k for kelvin. Fix: kilogram is kg; kelvin is K.
Pluralizing unit symbols or changing their case. Fix: symbols stay unchanged in plural forms; write 100 mm, not 100 mms.
Listing volume, area and density with incorrect powers or units. Fix: use m³, m² and kg m⁻³ respectively.

shortTheory.question: Q12.2. Why SI units are user friendly?
shortTheory.answer: SI units use base 10, just like our number system. So, it is much easier to learn, remember and convert these units.

shortTheory.question: Q12.3. Define systematic error and random error.
shortTheory.answer: Systematic errors may be removed by adding or subtracting a constant adjustment given to each measurement. Systematic error affect the accuracy of the measurement. Another type of error which a student commits during measurement is called a random error. Random error causes one measurement to differ slightly from the next measurement.

shortTheory.question: Q12.4. What is reason behind a random error?
shortTheory.answer: It comes from unpredictable changes during an experiment. The main reasons for random errors are limitations of instruments, environmental factors and slight variation in procedure.

shortTheory.question: Q12.5. Does systematic error affect the accuracy?
shortTheory.answer: Systematic error affect the accuracy of the measurement.

shortTheory.question: Q12.7. Define metre.
shortTheory.answer: It is the standard unit of length. Symbol m is used for metre. Metre is the distance travelled by light in vacuum in about 300 millionth of a second.

shortTheory.question: Q12.8. Mention two benefits scientists get by using SI units.
shortTheory.answer: The adoption of SI units is important in all branches of science because it makes communication easy worldwide. It allows scientists to share data easily.
